**The market-implied odds reflect the official NOAA observation at San Francisco International Airport (SFO), where the daily maximum reached 71°F on August 30, 2026, at 2:07 PM local time.** This places the outcome squarely in the 70-71°F bin, consistent with the 100% trader consensus.

The result aligned with a partly cloudy day under the influence of the marine layer and onshore flow from the cool California Current, though actual warming exceeded the pre-event National Weather Service forecast of a high near 66°F. The recorded value fell 3°F below the 1991-2020 normal of 74°F yet exceeded downtown San Francisco’s 65°F maximum, highlighting the typical airport-versus-urban microclimate difference driven by proximity to the bay and reduced urban heat retention. Historical context shows August 30 highs at SFO have varied widely, with a record of 91°F in 2023 and an average near 70°F in recent decades.

Trader positioning consolidated rapidly once preliminary reports confirmed the 71°F peak, as the market resolves strictly to the SFO station reading with limited scope for post-publication revisions. The only realistic challenges would involve an official data correction issued before the following day’s first observation or an unforeseen measurement anomaly, both of which carry low probability given standard NWS quality controls.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Benito Juárez International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

No strong offshore flow or high-pressure ridge is currently forecast to break this pattern and allow temperatures to reach the low 70s or above. The market’s heavy weighting on 68–69°F (44.5%) and 66–67°F (26.5%) therefore tracks the consensus forecast range, while lower probabilities for 70–71°F or higher capture residual model uncertainty around any late-day clearing or slight warming.

Traders are pricing in the typical late-summer moderation driven by ocean influence rather than anomalous heat, with resolution hinging on the official high reported for the day. Updated National Weather Service guidance or model runs tomorrow morning will be the key near-term catalyst.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus centers on a 23–24°C high for September 1 in Mexico City, reflecting model consensus and seasonal norms amid the rainy season.**

Mexico City’s high-elevation valley location (approximately 2,240 m) keeps daytime maxima moderate even in late summer. Historical September averages show daily highs near 23–24°C, with substantial rainfall and frequent afternoon thunderstorms that cap temperatures through cloud cover and evaporative cooling. Recent forecasts for September 1 consistently project highs of 22–24°C under partly cloudy skies with a high probability of thunderstorms, aligning closely with current conditions observed in late August.

These patterns explain why 24°C leads at 45.5% implied probability, followed by 23°C at 25.5%, while 25°C and 22°C hold smaller shares. Probabilities for 26°C or higher remain low (4%) because strong convective activity and seasonal moisture typically prevent significant excursions above the norm. Lower outcomes below 22°C are discounted given the absence of unusual cooling signals in model runs.

Upcoming National Meteorological Service or CONAGUA updates on the final 24-hour forecast will be the key near-term catalyst for any shifts in these market-implied odds.
